Pushed to main

All three F8 features are live and pushed to main (0b071d0), and every test passed. Before building, I amended the spec with your go-ahead:

  • Part A: the constitution goes to 2.0. Article VIII.2 gains the read-only share exception.
  • Part B: new FR-048 (share link), FR-054 (PDF) and FR-055 (booking-site links). FR-050 now includes the shared page. The two Out-of-scope lines are narrowed.
  • 004 and 006: the new API and UI requirements, tests and tasks F8.1–F8.5, with Changelog rows.
  • 1. Share link
  • API: POST /trips/{id}/share creates the link or returns the existing one; DELETE turns it off. Both are owner-only (anyone else gets 404), and a trip with no chosen plan gets 409.
  • Public GET /shared/{token}: returns exactly nine fields: name, cities, dates, people, budget, when the plan was made, and the plan without its internal hash. No chat, email, ids, versions, preferences, locks or excludes. Revoked or unknown tokens get 404, and it's limited to 60 requests a minute per address.
  • Token: 32 random bytes, stored unhashed. POST has to hand back the existing link, and a hash would only hide the link from someone who can already read the plan in the database. This is recorded in the Changelog.
  • Shared page /s/:token: read-only, with the trip name and facts, transport, hotel, day by day, map and budget. It's labelled "Shared plan · prices are estimates" and has "Plan your own trip" and "Download PDF". There's no chat, editing, versions or trade-offs. Search engines are told not to index it, both in the page and by an X-Robots-Tag header that production now sends. A dead link shows "This shared plan isn't available".
  • Plan detail: a "Share" button opens a dialog with Copy link (with a select-and-copy fallback) and Stop sharing.
  • 2. PDF: "Download PDF" opens the browser's print dialog, on Plan detail and on the shared page.
  • Printed: title, trip facts, transport and hotel, each day kept on one page, the budget table with "Estimated prices", black on white.
  • Hidden: header, chat, buttons, versions, trade-offs, the live-price links and the donut chart.
  • Map: it printed cleanly, so it stays, minus its zoom buttons.
  • 3. Live-price links: "Check live prices on <site> ↗" with "Tripwise doesn't book; prices there may differ." Each opens in a new tab with rel="noopener noreferrer", and the URL patterns are in config.yaml.
  • Hotel (Booking.com): prefilled with the city, dates, adults and rooms. The format is confirmed from Booking's own API docs and consistent public examples, not a live fetch, because the page needs JavaScript to render.
  • Flights and trains (MakeMyTrip), buses (redBus): these open the plain search page, by your rule. No published prefilled format turned up, and live fetches timed out.

Test results

  • API-AT-09: 4/4. The live API also showed the nine fields only, revoke → 404, and the link sites.
  • UI suite, both widths: 42 passed, 2 skipped (the live-Groq chat spec, which needs E2E_LIVE_GROQ=1).
  • New browser checks: copy link, open in a fresh logged-out browser, read-only view, axe on the shared page, stop sharing → not-available page; the print layout plus a real page.pdf(); link targets, rel, and the Booking.com city, dates, adults and rooms.
  • Backend: 117 passed. Build OK.
  • Deploys: backend and Vercel production.
  • DEP-AT-01 on the deployed site: passed in 18.0 s.

Generated PDFs stay out of git; the print-layout screenshots are committed. The transcript 1.md / transcript 2.md exports are still untracked in the repo root and were kept out of every commit.

Small UI fix (006 follow-up F9, spec first: UI-FR-02 + Changelog). The dates are validated only on submit; validate them as soon as either date changes:

  • 1. If the end date is before the start date: show "End date can't be before the start date." under End date right away, set aria-invalid, and mark the "(N days)" label as invalid (don't show a negative count).
  • 2. If the trip is shorter than 2 days or longer than 7: show "A trip lasts 2 to 7 days (start and end included)." right away, and show the day count in the error colour, e.g. "(15 days)".
  • 3. If the start date is earlier than tomorrow or more than 365 days ahead, show its existing message right away too.
  • 4. Clear each message as soon as the dates are fixed.
  • 5. Also help users avoid the mistake: set the End date picker's min to the start date and max to start + 6 days. If the start date moves past the end date, leave the end date as it is so the error shows; don't silently change it.
  • 6. Use the same rules and wording as the existing submit-time check (one shared function), and keep the server rules unchanged. Error text must be announced (role or aria-live via the existing FieldError) and meet AA contrast. Other fields keep validating on submit.

Tests: a Playwright check at 360 and 1280 px that picks an end date before the start date, then a 15-day range, and sees each message with no submit, and that both disappear after a valid range. Run the full UI suite, then deploy the frontend to Vercel production with the same VITE_API_URL. Commit and push.

Ran 1 shell command

Live dates on New trip now check themselves as they change, without waiting for submit. Production is serving it: the new message is in the live validate chunk on tripwise-inky.vercel.app, and everything is pushed to main (e7edbd4). The spec change to UI-FR-02 and its Changelog row were committed first.

What changed

  • One shared rule set: a new validateDates function checks the dates both when they change and on submit, with the same wording. Server rules are unchanged, and other fields still validate only on submit.
  • End before start: "End date can't be before the start date." appears under End date right away and the field is marked invalid. The day count shows "(check dates)" in the error colour instead of a negative number. On submit this case used to get the 2–7 days message; it now gets this one.
  • Outside 2–7 days: "A trip lasts 2 to 7 days (start and end included)." appears at once, and the count shows in the error colour, e.g. "(15 days)". That colour is about 7:1 on white, above AA.
  • Start date: the existing "tomorrow or later" and "within 365 days" messages also appear at once. The start picker now has a 365-day max as well.
  • Clearing: each message disappears as soon as the dates are valid.
  • Pickers: End date is limited to the start date through start + 6 days. If you move the start past the end, the end date stays where it is, so the message shows.
  • Announced errors: the shared field-error component now stays in the page as an aria-live="polite" region, so screen readers announce errors as they appear. This applies to every form field.

Tests

  • New date test, at 360 and 1280 px: an end date before the start, then a 15-day range, then a past start date. Each message appears without submitting and clears after a valid range, and moving the start past the end keeps the end and shows the message. Passed at both widths.
  • Full UI suite: 44 passed, 2 skipped (the live-Groq chat spec), at both widths with axe.

Pushed to main

All three F10 changes are live and pushed to main (7d5c336), and every suite passed. The spec changes (UI-FR-02, UI-FR-06, API-FR-06) were committed first. I also amended Part B's FR-046, since "My Trips lists upcoming and past trips" no longer held once trips with no plan are hidden; there's a Changelog row for it.

What changed

  • 1. Budget starts empty: the field is blank with the placeholder "e.g. 30000". Submitting it empty shows "Enter your budget." next to the field and focuses it, for both Total and Per person. A typed amount that isn't a whole number still gets the old "whole rupees" message. Duplicate and Edit budget still bring the trip's own budget.
  • 2. Trips with no plan are hidden: GET /trips leaves out infeasible trips. They stay in the database, the "Edit budget" screen right after planning still works, and opening one by URL still works.
  • 3. Newest first: both tabs are ordered by created_at, newest first (previously by start date), and the page shows the API's order unchanged.

Tests

  • API: the trips-list test now checks that infeasible trips are left out (but still open by id) and that both tabs are newest first. Backend: 117 passed.
  • New browser checks (f10-budget-list.spec.ts, 360 and 1280 px): an empty budget is blocked with its message and focus; of two planned trips and one infeasible trip, only the two planned ones are listed, newest first.
  • Updated tests: the keyboard-only run now types a budget, and two accessibility checks fill one in. These relied on the ₹30,000 default.
  • Full UI suite: 48 passed, 2 skipped (the live-Groq chat spec), at both widths with axe.
  • Keyboard test fix: one run of the keyboard test (UI-AT-08) failed to tab to "Skip for now". It passed 4/4 when repeated. The cause was a race in the test: it started tabbing as soon as the URL changed, before the Profile page had rendered. It now waits for each page to appear first.

Deploys

  • The first backend redeploy shipped the old code. That commit had failed (the quotes around "Enter your budget." broke the git command), and the deploy script ships committed code. I recommitted using a message file and redeployed.
  • Live check after redeploying: the list showed the newest trip first and left out the infeasible one, which still opened by id.
  • Frontend: Vercel production with the same VITE_API_URL.
  • DEP-AT-01: passed in 17.4 s on the redeployed site.

Owner UI change F11 (spec first: UI-FR-02 + Changelog). Frontend only.
New trip starts with no defaults in these four fields:

  • 1. Start date and End date: empty (no +30-day default).
  • Keep the date-picker limits: start from tomorrow to +365 days; end from the start date to start + 6 days once a start is chosen.
  • Show the "(N days)" count only when both dates are chosen.
  • The live date checks (F9) run only when both dates are filled. On submit, an empty one shows "Choose a start date." / "Choose an end date." next to it and focuses it.
  • 2. People: empty (no default 2). On submit, an empty one shows "Enter how many people are going (1–6)." The other people rules are unchanged.
  • 3. Budget: remove the "e.g. 30000" placeholder, so the field is plainly empty. The "Enter your budget." check stays.
  • 4. Duplicate and Edit budget still bring the trip's own dates, people and budget. Only a fresh New trip starts empty.

Tests:

  • A fresh New trip has empty start date, end date, people and budget, and no day count.
  • Submitting empty shows all four messages and focuses the first one.
  • Update the Playwright helpers and any spec that relied on the old date or people defaults: fillTrip must always set dates and people.

Run the full UI suite at 360 and 1280 px, then deploy the frontend to Vercel production with the same VITE_API_URL. Rerun DEP-AT-01, commit and push.

Pushed to main

F11 is live: a fresh New trip now opens with empty start date, end date, people and budget. Everything is pushed to main (3eba84a), and the UI-FR-02 spec change and its Changelog row were committed first.

What changed (frontend only)

  • Dates: no default any more (it was 30 days ahead). The picker limits stay: start from tomorrow to 365 days ahead; end from the start date to start + 6 once a start is chosen. The "(N days)" count only shows when both dates are filled, and the live date checks only start then.
  • People: no default of 2. An empty field gets "Enter how many people are going (1–6)."; the other people rules are unchanged.
  • Budget: the "e.g. 30000" placeholder is gone; "Enter your budget." still applies.
  • Messages on submit: an empty start date shows "Choose a start date.", an empty end date "Choose an end date.", and focus goes to the first field with a problem.
  • Duplicate and Edit budget still bring the trip's own dates, people and budget.

Tests

  • New f11-empty-fields.spec.ts (360 and 1280 px):
  • A fresh New trip has the four fields empty, no budget placeholder and no day count.
  • Submitting with only the cities and preferences shows all four messages, marks the four fields invalid and focuses Start date.
  • fillTrip helper: it now always sets dates and people, using a default only when a field is still empty. That way UI-AT-04's step-by-step changes aren't overwritten.
  • Keyboard-only test (UI-AT-08): it now types the dates and the number of people.
  • Test locale: the UI tests now run with locale en-IN and time zone Asia/Kolkata. Typed dates follow the locale's day-month-year order, and before this they depended on the test machine's settings.
  • Full UI suite: the first full run had 2 failures, both the F10 test still checking for the "e.g. 30000" placeholder this change removes. After updating that check, the clean full run was 50 passed, 2 skipped (the live-Groq chat spec), at both widths with axe.
  • Deploy: frontend to Vercel production with the same VITE_API_URL; the backend didn't change.
  • DEP-AT-01: passed in 15.6 s on the deployed site.
